newsitem.title: UK: Report defends recommended prices for electricals.
newsitem.headline: Report defends recommended prices for electricals.

text.p: A ban on recommended retail prices for electrical goods in Britain would not benefit the consumer and is as likely to result in higher prices as lower prices, according to a report published on Wednesday.

The report, commissioned by the British Radio and Electronic Equipment Manufacturers' Association (BREMA), found no evidence that recommended retail prices distorted the market for electrical goods or were anti-competitive.

The organisation commissioned the survey after details of a two-year Monopolies and Mergers Commission investigation into the electricals market were leaked to the press last month. This suggested the MMC wanted to ban recommended retail prices on electricals goods.
Trade minister Margaret Beckett is expected to decide whether or not to act on the MMC's recommendations in the next few weeks.
Earlier this month BREMA commissioned an opinion poll, conducted by MORI, which found that shoppers found recommended retail prices helpful and did not want them abolished.
